d1.types.title: Type c length and n
d1.types.reteach:
**Type c has length 1 unless you say otherwise.** `DATA x TYPE c.` then `x = 'ABC'.` leaves `A`. Nothing warns you; the text is cut to fit.

Fix: give a length (`TYPE c LENGTH 10`) or use `string` when the size is unknown.

**Type n** is text that only holds digits and pads with leading zeros: `n LENGTH 5` with `'42'` is `00042`. It is for codes (postal codes, material numbers), not for calculating.

extra.brief: Predict, then run: `DATA a TYPE c LENGTH 3. a = 'ABCDE'. WRITE a.` and `DATA z TYPE n LENGTH 4. z = '7'. WRITE z.`

d1.decl.title: DATA, CONSTANTS, TYPES
d1.decl.reteach:
`DATA` = a variable (has memory, can change).
`CONSTANTS` = a value that never changes; it **needs VALUE** and any assignment is a syntax error you see at once.
`TYPES` = only a shape. `TYPES ty_amt TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2.` creates no variable. You then write `DATA gv_a TYPE ty_amt.`

Why TYPES at all? Change one line and every variable of that type changes with it.

extra.brief: Declare a type `ty_qty` (p, length 6, 1 decimal), two variables of that type and a constant `gc_max` = 100. Try assigning to the constant and read the error.
extra.solution: `TYPES ty_qty TYPE p LENGTH 6 DECIMALS 1. DATA: gv_a TYPE ty_qty, gv_b TYPE ty_qty. CONSTANTS gc_max TYPE i VALUE 100.` Assigning `gc_max = 5.` gives a syntax error on Check (Ctrl+F2).

d1.struct.title: Structures
d1.struct.reteach:
A structure is **one record** with named fields. Define the shape with `TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_emp, … END OF ty_emp.` and create a variable `DATA gs_emp TYPE ty_emp.`

Read and write a field with a dash: `gs_emp-name = 'Asha'.` The dash, not a dot or arrow, separates structure and field.

`CLEAR gs_emp.` resets every field at once.

extra.brief: Create `ty_book` with title (c 30), pages (i) and price (p 8,2). Fill one variable and print it, then CLEAR it and print again.

d1.inline.title: Inline declarations
d1.inline.reteach:
`DATA(lv_n) = 10.` declares `lv_n` and fills it; the type comes from the **right-hand side**. 10 is an integer, so `lv_n` is type i.

Trap: `DATA(lv_t) = 'Hi'.` gives a c of **length 2**. Assigning `'Hello'` later keeps only `He`. When the text can grow, declare `DATA lv_s TYPE string.` (or write the literal in backticks).

extra.brief: Write `DATA(a) = 5.` and `DATA(b) = 'AB'.`, and declare `DATA c TYPE string.` with the value AB. Then assign 'ABCDEF' to b and c and print both.
extra.solution: b prints AB (c length 2), c prints ABCDEF (string).

d2.intmath.title: Integer arithmetic and rounding
d2.intmath.reteach:
When the target is **i**, the answer is a whole number and ABAP **rounds** (half away from zero): `gv_int = 7 / 2.` gives **4**, and `gv_int = 10 / 4.` gives **3** (2.5 rounds to 3).

Want the cut-off instead? Use `DIV`: `7 DIV 2` = 3. Want the remainder? `MOD`: `7 MOD 2` = 1.

When decimals matter, make the target a **p** with DECIMALS: then `7 / 2` = 3.50.

extra.brief: Predict, then run: `DATA i TYPE i. i = 9 / 2. WRITE i.` and `WRITE / 9 DIV 2. WRITE / 9 MOD 2.`
extra.solution: 9 / 2 = 4.5 rounds to 5; DIV gives 4; MOD gives 1.

d2.divmod.title: DIV, MOD and decimals
d2.divmod.reteach:
`DIV` = whole-number quotient, `MOD` = remainder. Together they rebuild the number: `( 17 DIV 5 ) * 5 + 17 MOD 5` = 17.

Common uses: every nth item (`sy-index MOD 3 = 0`), even/odd (`MOD 2`), turning 125 minutes into 2 hours and 5 minutes (`125 DIV 60`, `125 MOD 60`).

For **decimals** use a **p** variable with DECIMALS; **i** can never hold a fraction.

extra.brief: Turn 3725 seconds into hours, minutes and seconds with DIV and MOD only.
extra.solution: 3725 DIV 3600 = 1 hour; (3725 MOD 3600) DIV 60 = 2 minutes; 3725 MOD 60 = 5 seconds.

d2.strings.title: CONCATENATE, CONDENSE, templates, strlen
d2.strings.reteach:
Join: `CONCATENATE a b INTO c SEPARATED BY space.` or, preferred, a template `|{ a } { b }|`.
`CONDENSE c.` trims both ends and shrinks inner runs of spaces to one (changes the variable itself).
`strlen( c )` counts characters (trailing blanks of a c field do not count).

Case: `to_upper( c )` and `to_lower( c )`.

extra.brief: Build "SAP ABAP 2026" from three separate variables using a template, then print its length.
extra.solution: `DATA(lv) = |{ a } { b } { c }|. WRITE strlen( lv ).` gives 14.

d2.offset.title: Offset, length and CS/CP
d2.offset.reteach:
`lv+3(4)`: skip 3 characters, take 4. The first character is at offset **0**.
`CS` means "contains string" and ignores case; on success `sy-fdpos` holds the offset where it was found.
`CP` is pattern match: `*` any characters, `+` one character. `'SAPABAP' CP 'SAP*'` is true.

For safety, check the length first: asking for more characters than exist is a runtime error.

extra.brief: Does `'invoice_2026' CP 'invoice*'` hold? What does `'invoice_2026' CS 'VOICE'` give and what is sy-fdpos?
extra.solution: Both are true; sy-fdpos = 2 (position of "voice" after "in").

d3.ifcase.title: IF, ELSEIF and CASE
d3.ifcase.reteach:
Conditions are checked top to bottom; the **first true branch runs** and the rest are skipped. Put the most specific test first (for FizzBuzz: multiple of 15 before 3 and 5).

`CASE` tests one variable against many values and needs `WHEN OTHERS` for everything else. Compare with `=` or `EQ`; not-equal is `<>` or `NE`.

Combine tests with `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` and group them with parentheses (spaces around each).

extra.brief: Write a CASE that prints "weekend" for sy-datum-based day 6 or 7 (use `lv_day = 6.` by hand) and "weekday" otherwise.
extra.solution: `CASE lv_day. WHEN 6 OR 7. WRITE 'weekend'. WHEN OTHERS. WRITE 'weekday'. ENDCASE.`

d3.do.title: DO, WHILE and sy-index
d3.do.reteach:
`DO n TIMES.` runs n passes. A bare `DO.` never stops by itself, so it **must** contain an `EXIT`.
`sy-index` is the pass counter and **starts at 1** (not 0). After `DO 3 TIMES.` the passes are 1, 2, 3.
`WHILE cond.` tests **before** each pass, so it may run zero times.

extra.brief: Print the powers of 2 below 1000 using WHILE.
extra.solution: `DATA lv TYPE i VALUE 1. WHILE lv < 1000. WRITE / lv. lv = lv * 2. ENDWHILE.` prints 1 2 4 … 512.

d3.exit.title: EXIT, CONTINUE and CHECK
d3.exit.reteach:
`EXIT` ends the **loop you are in**. In nested loops that is only the innermost one; the outer loop carries on.
`CONTINUE` abandons only the current pass.
`CHECK cond.` means "carry on only if cond is true", otherwise it behaves like CONTINUE inside a loop.

Outside any loop, `EXIT` leaves the whole processing block (for example the event block), which surprises many beginners.

extra.brief: Predict how many lines print: an outer `DO 3 TIMES.` containing an inner `DO 5 TIMES.` that does `EXIT.` when sy-index = 3 after writing the index.
extra.solution: The inner loop writes 2 lines per outer pass (indexes 1 and 2) and exits at 3, so 3 x 2 = 6 lines.

d3.nested.title: Nested loops and sy-index
d3.nested.reteach:
Each loop has its own `sy-index`. While the inner loop runs, `sy-index` is the inner count; once it ends, the outer count is visible again.

If you need the outer number inside the inner loop, **copy it into a variable first**: `lv_row = sy-index.`

Cost: 10 x 10 passes = 100 executions; nested loops grow fast, which matters again with big tables.

extra.brief: Print all pairs (i, j) with i from 1 to 3 and j from 1 to 2. How many lines? In what order?
extra.solution: 6 lines: 1 1, 1 2, 2 1, 2 2, 3 1, 3 2. The inner counter changes fastest.

d4.declare.title: Declaring and filling a table
d4.declare.reteach:
A table needs a **row type** (a structure) first: `TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_emp … END OF ty_emp.` Then `DATA gt_emp TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_emp WITH EMPTY KEY.`

The **work area** `DATA gs_emp TYPE ty_emp.` is the single row you read or build. `APPEND gs_emp TO gt_emp.` adds it as the last row; `APPEND VALUE #( … ) TO gt_emp.` builds and adds in one statement.

The table and the work area are two different things: the work area is **not** a row of the table.

extra.brief: Define ty_city (name c20, population i). Build a table with three cities, then print lines( ).
extra.solution: Declare ty_city and `gt_city`, append three rows with VALUE #( … ), then `WRITE lines( gt_city ).` prints 3.

d4.loopcopy.title: LOOP AT … INTO copies the row
d4.loopcopy.reteach:
`LOOP AT gt INTO gs.` **copies** each row into `gs`. The table row and the work area are separate memory.

So `gs-salary = gs-salary + 1000.` inside the loop changes only the copy. When the loop ends the table is exactly as before.

To persist the change: `MODIFY gt FROM gs.` (current row). The other way is a field symbol, which points at the real row (Day 8).

extra.brief: Loop over a 3-row table adding 5 to a number field without MODIFY, print the table, then add MODIFY and print again.
extra.solution: First print shows unchanged values; with MODIFY the values are +5.

d4.modify.title: MODIFY and DELETE rows
d4.modify.reteach:
`MODIFY gt FROM gs.` inside a `LOOP AT gt INTO gs` overwrites the **current** row with the work area.
Outside a loop give the row: `MODIFY gt FROM gs INDEX 3.`
`DELETE gt INDEX 2.` removes row 2; rows below move up by one, so row numbers change.

Never delete from a table inside a loop over it unless you understand the index shift; collect first, then delete (or use `DELETE gt WHERE …`).

extra.brief: Remove all rows with salary below 40000 using `DELETE gt_emp WHERE salary < 40000.` and print what is left.
extra.solution: Imran (38000) is removed; four rows remain.

d4.tabix.title: sy-tabix, lines( ) and sy-subrc
d4.tabix.reteach:
`sy-tabix` = row number inside a table loop (1, 2, 3 …), even when `WHERE` skips rows.
`lines( gt )` = how many rows the table has right now.
After `LOOP … ENDLOOP.` the `sy-subrc` is 0 if at least one row was processed and **4** if none was.

`sy-index` is for DO/WHILE; `sy-tabix` is for table loops. Do not mix them up.

extra.brief: Print `sy-tabix` for each row where salary > 50000 in the 5-row table, and the value of sy-subrc after the loop on an empty table.
extra.solution: Rows 2, 3, 5 print (the real positions); on an empty table sy-subrc is 4.

days.title: Data types and declarations
days.goal: Declare variables, constants, types and structures correctly, and know exactly how long each one is.
objectives: State the default length of type c and what happens when a longer text is assigned
Use n, i, p, string, d, t for the right job
Tell DATA, CONSTANTS and TYPES apart
Build and use a structure
Use inline declarations and know what type they get
days.read:
## The idea
Every variable in ABAP has a **type** that fixes what it can hold and how long it is. Most beginner bugs in ABAP come from guessing a type or a length.

## Elementary types you will use every day
- **c** — fixed-length text. `DATA x TYPE c.` has **length 1**, not "any length". Write `TYPE c LENGTH 20` for 20 characters. Assigning a longer text silently **cuts it off**.
- **string** — text of any length. Use it when you do not know the size.
- **n** — a *number-text*: only digits, stored as characters, padded with leading zeros (`'42'` in a `n LENGTH 5` becomes `00042`). Use it for codes such as postal codes, not for arithmetic.
- **i** — whole numbers (about ±2 billion).
- **p** — packed number with decimals: `TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2`. Use it for money and quantities.
- **d** (date, `YYYYMMDD`) and **t** (time, `HHMMSS`).

## DATA, CONSTANTS, TYPES
- `DATA` reserves memory for a variable.
- `CONSTANTS` reserves memory for a value that **cannot change**; it needs a `VALUE`, and assigning to it is a syntax error.
- `TYPES` only **describes** a shape. No memory is reserved until you write `DATA x TYPE that_type`.

## Structures
A structure is one record with several named fields. Define it once with `TYPES BEGIN OF … END OF`, then create a variable of that type and reach each field with a dash: `gs_emp-name`.

## Inline declarations (S/4HANA)
`DATA(lv_x) = 5.` declares and fills a variable in one step; the type is taken from the right side. Careful: `DATA(lv_t) = 'Hi'.` gives a **c of length 2**, so a longer text assigned later is cut off. For a text that can grow, use a string: write the literal in backticks, or declare `DATA lv_s TYPE string.`

## Naming habit
`gv_` global variable, `lv_` local, `gs_` structure, `gt_` table, `gc_` constant, `ty_` type. Readers (and interviewers) notice.

examples.title: Length of c
examples.code:
```abap
DATA gv_long  TYPE c LENGTH 20.
DATA gv_short TYPE c.

gv_long  = 'Deepak'.
gv_short = 'Deepak'.

WRITE: / gv_long.   "Deepak
WRITE: / gv_short.  "D   (length 1: the rest is cut off)
```
examples.notes: No error, no warning: the text is just truncated. This is the classic type c trap.

examples.title: n keeps leading zeros
examples.code:
```abap
DATA gv_zip TYPE n LENGTH 6.
gv_zip = '1234'.
WRITE: / gv_zip.    "001234
```
examples.notes: Digits only. Anything that is not a digit is dropped on assignment.

examples.title: TYPES describes, DATA allocates, CONSTANTS stays fixed
examples.code:
```abap
TYPES ty_amount TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2.   " only a description
DATA  gv_price  TYPE ty_amount.               " real variable
CONSTANTS gc_tax TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2 VALUE '0.18'.

gv_price = '19.99'.
" gc_tax = '0.20'.   <- syntax error: constants cannot change
```
examples.notes: Reuse one TYPES in many DATA lines so a change of length happens in one place.

examples.title: A structure
examples.code:
```abap
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_item,
         code  TYPE n LENGTH 6,
         name  TYPE c LENGTH 20,
         price TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2,
       END OF ty_item.

DATA gs_item TYPE ty_item.
gs_item-code = '1234'.
gs_item-name = 'Keyboard'.
WRITE: / gs_item-code, gs_item-name.
```
examples.notes: One variable, three fields. You will use this shape for every table row later.

exercise.title: Declare, fill and print
exercise.brief: In SAP Logon create a new program and prove to yourself how types and lengths behave.
steps: Open transaction **SE38**. Program name **ZABAP_D1** (Z or Y names are customer namespace). Create → type **Executable program** → save as **Local object** ($TMP).

Declare: a text of length 20 holding your name; a second text declared **without LENGTH**; a **n LENGTH 6**; a structure **ty_item** (code n6, name c20, price p 8 decimals 2); a constant **gc_tax** = 0.18; and **gv_total** as p 8 decimals 2.
Assign your name to **both** text variables, set the item to code 1234, name Keyboard, price 19.99, and compute **gv_total = price * ( 1 + gc_tax )**.
Print every value with WRITE, one per line.
Activate (**Ctrl+F3**) and run (**F8**). Compare with the expected output below.
expect: Name line shows your full name
The no-LENGTH text shows only the **first letter**
hints: Use `DATA gv_letter TYPE c.` for the one-letter variable and assign your name to it.
Write the formula as `gv_total = gs_item-price * ( 1 + gc_tax ).` Spaces around every parenthesis and operator are mandatory in ABAP.
exercise.solution:
```abap
REPORT zabap_d1.

CONSTANTS gc_tax TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2 VALUE '0.18'.

TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_item,
         code  TYPE n LENGTH 6,
         name  TYPE c LENGTH 20,
         price TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2,
       END OF ty_item.

DATA gv_name   TYPE c LENGTH 20.
DATA gv_letter TYPE c.
DATA gs_item   TYPE ty_item.
DATA gv_total  TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2.

gv_name   = 'Deepak'.
gv_letter = 'Deepak'.
gs_item-code  = '1234'.
gs_item-name  = 'Keyboard'.
gs_item-price = '19.99'.
gv_total = gs_item-price * ( 1 + gc_tax ).

WRITE: / 'Name  :', gv_name.
WRITE: / 'Letter:', gv_letter.
WRITE: / 'Code  :', gs_item-code.
WRITE: / 'Price :', gs_item-price.
WRITE: / 'Tax   :', gc_tax.
WRITE: / 'Total :', gv_total.
```

stretch.brief: Add `DATA(lv_text) = 'Hello'.` then assign `'Hello world'` to it and print it. Predict the output first, then explain it. Fix it so the full text survives.
stretch.solution: lv_text is type c length 5, so the output is "Hello". Declare `DATA lv_text TYPE string.` and the full "Hello world" is kept.

days.milestone: You can declare any basic variable, constant and structure without looking anything up.

days.title: Operators and strings
days.goal: Calculate correctly with integers and decimals, and handle text with the everyday string tools.
objectives: Predict integer arithmetic including rounding, DIV and MOD
Get decimals by using a p variable
Join, trim and measure text
Cut parts of text with offset and length
Compare text with CS and CP
days.read:
## Arithmetic and the result type
`+ - * /` and `**` (power) work as you expect, but **the type of the target decides how the answer looks**:
- into an **i** variable, `7 / 2` is **rounded** to **4** (not cut to 3);
- into a **p** variable with 2 decimals, `7 / 2` is **3.50**.

Whole-number division and remainder have their own operators: `7 DIV 2` = **3**, `7 MOD 2` = **1**. They are what you use for "every 3rd row", even/odd checks and splitting seconds into minutes.

Every operator needs spaces around it: `a+b` is wrong, `a + b` is right.

## Text tools
- Join: `CONCATENATE a b INTO c SEPARATED BY space.` or a **string template** `|Hello { lv_name }|`. Templates are the modern default.
- Length: `strlen( lv )`.
- Clean up: `CONDENSE lv.` removes leading and trailing spaces and shrinks runs of spaces to one. `to_upper( lv )` / `to_lower( lv )` change case.
- Replace: `replace( val = lv sub = 'a' with = 'b' occ = 0 )` (occ = 0 means all).
- **Offset and length**: `lv+3(4)` means "start after 3 characters, take 4". Counting starts at **0**.

## Comparing text
- `CS` contains string, **not** case-sensitive. It fills `sy-fdpos` with the position found.
- `CP` matches a pattern: `*` is any run of characters, `+` exactly one.
- `=` compares case-sensitively and ignores trailing blanks in c fields.

## Habit
When the result must keep decimals, **declare the target as p**, never i.

examples.title: Rounding, DIV, MOD
examples.code:
```abap
DATA: gv_int TYPE i, gv_div TYPE i, gv_mod TYPE i.
DATA gv_dec TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2.

gv_int = 7 / 2.     " 4  (rounded, not 3)
gv_dec = 7 / 2.     " 3.50
gv_div = 7 DIV 2.   " 3
gv_mod = 7 MOD 2.   " 1
WRITE: / gv_int, / gv_dec.
WRITE: / gv_div, / gv_mod.   " 3 and 1
```
examples.notes: Same expression, different targets, different answers. This is the integer-arithmetic trap.

examples.title: Join and template
examples.code:
```abap
DATA: gv_first TYPE c LENGTH 10 VALUE 'Deepak',
      gv_last  TYPE c LENGTH 10 VALUE 'Raj',
      gv_full  TYPE string.

CONCATENATE gv_first gv_last INTO gv_full SEPARATED BY space.
WRITE: / gv_full.                       " Deepak Raj
gv_full = |Welcome, { gv_first }!|.
WRITE: / gv_full.                       " Welcome, Deepak!
```
examples.notes: In templates, trailing blanks of a c field are not added.

examples.title: Clean and measure
examples.code:
```abap
DATA gv_messy TYPE string VALUE `   too   many    spaces  `.
CONDENSE gv_messy.
WRITE: / gv_messy.             " too many spaces
WRITE: / strlen( gv_messy ).   " 15
```
examples.notes: CONDENSE changes the variable itself. NO-GAPS would remove every space.

examples.title: Offset and CS
examples.code:
```abap
DATA gv_code TYPE c LENGTH 7 VALUE 'SAPABAP'.
WRITE: / gv_code+0(3).   " SAP
WRITE: / gv_code+3(4).   " ABAP

IF gv_code CS 'abap'.
  WRITE: / 'found at', sy-fdpos.   " found at 3
ENDIF.
```
examples.notes: Offset 3 means three characters skipped. CS ignores case, so 'abap' matches.

exercise.title: Numbers and names
exercise.brief: Prove the rounding rule and build a small text-cleaning program.
steps: Create **ZABAP_D2** in SE38.
Calculate **7 / 2** into an **i** variable and into a **p** (8, 2 decimals) variable, and also print **7 DIV 2** and **7 MOD 2**.
Join first name and last name (your own) with one space into a string and also build a greeting with a string template.
Store the text <three spaces>too<three spaces>many<four spaces>spaces<two spaces> in a string (use a backtick literal), CONDENSE it, and print it and its length.
Take **'SAPABAP'** and print the first three characters and the last four using offset/length.
Test whether your full name contains 'raj' with **CS**, and print the position from **sy-fdpos**.
expect: Integer result **4**; decimal result **3.50**; DIV **3**; MOD **1**
Full name and greeting both correct
CS true (it ignores case) and a position number printed
hints: Use two targets: `DATA gv_int TYPE i.` and `DATA gv_dec TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2.` and assign the same `7 / 2` to both.
Declare it TYPE string and write the literal in backticks (the key left of 1) so the spaces are kept; single quotes would drop trailing blanks.
Offset counting starts at 0: first three = `lv+0(3)`, last four = `lv+3(4)`.
exercise.solution:
```abap
REPORT zabap_d2.

DATA: gv_int   TYPE i,
      gv_div   TYPE i,
      gv_mod   TYPE i,
      gv_dec   TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2,
      gv_first TYPE c LENGTH 10 VALUE 'Deepak',
      gv_last  TYPE c LENGTH 10 VALUE 'Raj',
      gv_full  TYPE string,
      gv_greet TYPE string,
      gv_messy TYPE string VALUE `   too   many    spaces  `,
      gv_code  TYPE c LENGTH 7 VALUE 'SAPABAP'.

gv_int = 7 / 2.
gv_dec = 7 / 2.
gv_div = 7 DIV 2.
gv_mod = 7 MOD 2.
WRITE: / gv_int, / gv_dec, / gv_div, / gv_mod.

CONCATENATE gv_first gv_last INTO gv_full SEPARATED BY space.
gv_greet = |Welcome, { gv_first }!|.
WRITE: / gv_full, / gv_greet.

CONDENSE gv_messy.
WRITE: / gv_messy, / strlen( gv_messy ).

WRITE: / gv_code+0(3), / gv_code+3(4).

IF gv_full CS 'raj'.
  WRITE: / 'found at', sy-fdpos.
ENDIF.
```

stretch.brief: Use `replace( )` to turn "Deepak Raj" into "Deepak-Raj", and `to_upper( )` to print it in capitals. Then write one line that prints how many characters your full name has.
stretch.solution: `gv_full = replace( val = gv_full sub = ' ' with = '-' occ = 0 ).`  `WRITE / to_upper( gv_full ).`  `WRITE / strlen( gv_full ).`

days.milestone: You can predict integer vs decimal results and clean and slice text without trial and error.

days.title: Control flow and loops
days.goal: Make decisions and repeat work with IF, CASE, DO and WHILE, and control a loop with EXIT, CONTINUE and CHECK.
objectives: Write IF/ELSEIF and CASE correctly
Use DO n TIMES, DO and WHILE
Know that sy-index starts at 1
Know exactly what EXIT, CONTINUE and CHECK do
Handle nested loops
days.read:
## Decisions
`IF … ELSEIF … ELSE … ENDIF.` compares with `=` (or `EQ`), `<>` (`NE`), `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, and combines conditions with `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`.
`CASE x. WHEN 1. … WHEN OTHERS. … ENDCASE.` is cleaner when one variable is tested against many values. Always add `WHEN OTHERS`.

## Loops
- `DO n TIMES.` repeats n times.
- `DO.` repeats **forever** until something ends it (`EXIT`). Without an exit it never stops.
- `WHILE condition.` repeats while the condition is true.

Inside `DO` the system variable **`sy-index`** counts passes, **starting at 1**. Inside a table loop the counterpart is `sy-tabix` (Day 4).

## Steering a loop
- **`EXIT.`** leaves the loop **completely**. In nested loops it leaves **only the innermost** one; the outer loop continues.
- **`CONTINUE.`** skips the rest of this pass and starts the next.
- **`CHECK condition.`** is a shortcut: if the condition is **false**, behave like CONTINUE (inside a loop).

## Nested loops
The inner loop has its own `sy-index`. When the inner loop ends, the outer `sy-index` is back to the outer count.

## Success check
Most statements set **`sy-subrc`**: **0 means success**, anything else means "not found / failed". You will test it constantly from Day 6 on.

examples.title: IF and CASE
examples.code:
```abap
DATA gv_mark TYPE i VALUE 72.

IF gv_mark >= 80.
  WRITE: / 'Distinction'.
ELSEIF gv_mark >= 60.
  WRITE: / 'First class'.
ELSE.
  WRITE: / 'Below'.
ENDIF.

CASE sy-datum+4(2).        " the month part of today
  WHEN '10'.  WRITE: / 'October'.
  WHEN OTHERS. WRITE: / 'Another month'.
ENDCASE.
```
examples.notes: The first matching branch runs, the rest are skipped.

examples.title: DO with sy-index and EXIT
examples.code:
```abap
DO.
  IF sy-index > 5.
    EXIT.
  ENDIF.
  WRITE: / sy-index.   " 1 2 3 4 5
ENDDO.
```
examples.notes: A plain DO has no stop of its own. The EXIT is what makes it finite.

examples.title: EXIT leaves only the inner loop
examples.code:
```abap
DO 3 TIMES.
  DATA(lv_outer) = sy-index.
  DO 3 TIMES.
    IF sy-index = 2.
      EXIT.             " leaves the inner DO only
    ENDIF.
    WRITE: / lv_outer, sy-index.
  ENDDO.
ENDDO.
" prints 1 1 / 2 1 / 3 1
```
examples.notes: The outer loop still runs all 3 passes; each inner loop stops at its second pass.

examples.title: CONTINUE
examples.code:
```abap
DO 6 TIMES.
  IF sy-index MOD 2 = 0.
    CONTINUE.            " skip even numbers
  ENDIF.
  WRITE: / sy-index.     " 1 3 5
ENDDO.
```
examples.notes: CONTINUE does not leave the loop; it jumps to the next pass.

exercise.title: Loops that behave
exercise.brief: Four small loop problems, all in one program.
steps: Create **ZABAP_D3**.
**FizzBuzz 1–15:** print Fizz for multiples of 3, Buzz for multiples of 5, FizzBuzz for both, otherwise the number. Use DO and MOD.
**Sum 1–100** with DO 100 TIMES. Print it (it must be 5050).
**First n whose square is above 500:** use a plain DO and EXIT. Print n.
**CONTINUE:** print the numbers 1 to 10 that are not multiples of 3.
Activate and run. Compare with the expected output.
expect: FizzBuzz lines: 1, 2, Fizz, 4, Buzz, Fizz, 7, 8, Fizz, Buzz, 11, Fizz, 13, 14, FizzBuzz
First n **23** (22 squared is 484, 23 squared is 529)
hints: Check FizzBuzz first (multiple of 15), otherwise the 3 and 5 branches would catch it earlier.
Add to the sum with `gv_sum = gv_sum + sy-index.` inside the DO.
For the square: `IF sy-index * sy-index > 500.` then store sy-index in a variable and `EXIT.`
exercise.solution:
```abap
REPORT zabap_d3.

DATA: gv_sum TYPE i,
      gv_n   TYPE i.

DO 15 TIMES.
  IF sy-index MOD 15 = 0.
    WRITE: / 'FizzBuzz'.
  ELSEIF sy-index MOD 3 = 0.
    WRITE: / 'Fizz'.
  ELSEIF sy-index MOD 5 = 0.
    WRITE: / 'Buzz'.
  ELSE.
    WRITE: / sy-index.
  ENDIF.
ENDDO.

DO 100 TIMES.
  gv_sum = gv_sum + sy-index.
ENDDO.
WRITE: / 'Sum:', gv_sum.

DO.
  IF sy-index * sy-index > 500.
    gv_n = sy-index.
    EXIT.
  ENDIF.
ENDDO.
WRITE: / 'First n:', gv_n.

DO 10 TIMES.
  IF sy-index MOD 3 = 0.
    CONTINUE.
  ENDIF.
  WRITE: / sy-index.
ENDDO.
```

stretch.brief: Print a 5 x 5 multiplication table using two nested DO loops. Keep the outer number in a variable, because sy-index belongs to the inner loop while it runs.
stretch.solution: Outer: `DO 5 TIMES. lv_row = sy-index. DO 5 TIMES. lv_prod = lv_row * sy-index. WRITE lv_prod. ENDDO. SKIP. ENDDO.` Declare `lv_prod TYPE i` and write each product with a width, e.g. `WRITE (4) lv_prod.`

days.milestone: You can write and trace any loop with a known number of passes and explain exactly where EXIT leaves.

days.title: Internal tables, part 1
days.goal: Create an internal table, fill it, loop over it, change rows safely and count them.
objectives: Declare a standard internal table from a structure type
Fill it with APPEND
Explain that LOOP AT … INTO copies each row
Change rows with MODIFY
Use sy-tabix and lines( )
days.read:
## What an internal table is
An **internal table** is a list of rows held in memory while the program runs. Every row has the same structure. It is ABAP's main working container: you read database rows into one, process it, then show it.

## Declaring one
First a row type, then the table:
`TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_emp, … END OF ty_emp.`
`DATA gt_emp TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_emp WITH EMPTY KEY.`
`DATA gs_emp TYPE ty_emp.`  ← the **work area**: one row you hold in your hand.

## Filling
- `APPEND gs_emp TO gt_emp.` adds the work area as a new last row.
- `APPEND VALUE #( id = 2 name = 'Ravi' ) TO gt_emp.` builds the row in place (modern, shorter).

## Reading rows with a loop
`LOOP AT gt_emp INTO gs_emp. … ENDLOOP.` visits each row in order. **INTO copies the row into the work area.** So:
- you can read the work area freely;
- changing `gs_emp-salary` inside the loop does **not** change the table. Write it back with `MODIFY gt_emp FROM gs_emp.` (inside the loop this updates the current row).

Inside a loop `sy-tabix` is the current row number (starting at 1). `sy-subrc` is 4 after the loop if the table had no rows to visit.

## Counting and clearing
`lines( gt_emp )` returns the row count. `CLEAR gt_emp.` empties the table. `DELETE gt_emp INDEX 2.` removes row 2. `WHERE` filters: `LOOP AT gt_emp INTO gs_emp WHERE salary > 50000.`

## Habits
Name tables `gt_/lt_` and work areas `gs_/ls_`. Header lines (a table with a built-in work area) are obsolete; do not use them.

examples.title: Declare and fill
examples.code:
```abap
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_emp,
         id     TYPE i,
         name   TYPE c LENGTH 15,
         salary TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2,
       END OF ty_emp.

DATA gt_emp TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_emp WITH EMPTY KEY.
DATA gs_emp TYPE ty_emp.

gs_emp-id = 1. gs_emp-name = 'Asha'. gs_emp-salary = 42000.
APPEND gs_emp TO gt_emp.

APPEND VALUE #( id = 2 name = 'Ravi' salary = 55000 ) TO gt_emp.
```
examples.notes: The same table now holds two rows.

examples.title: LOOP … INTO copies the row
examples.code:
```abap
LOOP AT gt_emp INTO gs_emp.
  gs_emp-salary = gs_emp-salary + 1000.   " changes only the copy
ENDLOOP.
" gt_emp is unchanged here!
```
examples.notes: This is the exact point the diagnostic caught: the work area is a copy.

examples.title: MODIFY writes the copy back
examples.code:
```abap
LOOP AT gt_emp INTO gs_emp.
  gs_emp-salary = gs_emp-salary + 1000.
  MODIFY gt_emp FROM gs_emp.             " updates the current row
ENDLOOP.
```
examples.notes: Day 8 shows field symbols, which edit the row directly without copying.

examples.title: sy-tabix, lines and WHERE
examples.code:
```abap
LOOP AT gt_emp INTO gs_emp WHERE salary > 50000.
  WRITE: / sy-tabix, gs_emp-name.
ENDLOOP.
WRITE: / 'Rows:', lines( gt_emp ).
```
examples.notes: sy-tabix is the row number in the full table, even when WHERE skips some rows.

exercise.title: Employee table
exercise.brief: Build a five-row table, report on it, then give everyone a raise the right way.
steps: Create **ZABAP_D4**.
Define **ty_emp** (id i, name c15, salary p 8,2) and a standard table **gt_emp**.
Add five employees: Asha 42000, Ravi 55000, Meena 61000, Imran 38000, Sara 70000.
Loop and print row number, name and salary. In the same loop add up the **total salary** and count employees earning **above 50000**.
Print the total, the count and the number of rows with **lines( )**.
Second loop: raise every salary by **10%** and write it back with **MODIFY**. Loop again and print the new salaries.
expect: Rows 1 to 5 with names and salaries
After the raise: Asha 46,200 · Ravi 60,500 · Meena 67,100 · Imran 41,800 · Sara 77,000
hints: Use `APPEND VALUE #( id = 2 name = 'Ravi' salary = 55000 ) TO gt_emp.` for each row.
If the second listing shows the old salaries, you forgot `MODIFY gt_emp FROM gs_emp.`
exercise.solution:
```abap
REPORT zabap_d4.

TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_emp,
         id     TYPE i,
         name   TYPE c LENGTH 15,
         salary TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2,
       END OF ty_emp.

DATA: gt_emp   TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_emp WITH EMPTY KEY,
      gs_emp   TYPE ty_emp,
      gv_total TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2,
      gv_high  TYPE i.

APPEND VALUE #( id = 1 name = 'Asha'  salary = 42000 ) TO gt_emp.
APPEND VALUE #( id = 2 name = 'Ravi'  salary = 55000 ) TO gt_emp.
APPEND VALUE #( id = 3 name = 'Meena' salary = 61000 ) TO gt_emp.
APPEND VALUE #( id = 4 name = 'Imran' salary = 38000 ) TO gt_emp.
APPEND VALUE #( id = 5 name = 'Sara'  salary = 70000 ) TO gt_emp.

LOOP AT gt_emp INTO gs_emp.
  WRITE: / sy-tabix, gs_emp-name, gs_emp-salary.
  gv_total = gv_total + gs_emp-salary.
  IF gs_emp-salary > 50000.
    gv_high = gv_high + 1.
  ENDIF.
ENDLOOP.
WRITE: / 'Total:', gv_total, 'Above 50000:', gv_high, 'Rows:', lines( gt_emp ).

LOOP AT gt_emp INTO gs_emp.
  gs_emp-salary = gs_emp-salary * 11 / 10.
  MODIFY gt_emp FROM gs_emp.
ENDLOOP.

SKIP.
LOOP AT gt_emp INTO gs_emp.
  WRITE: / gs_emp-name, gs_emp-salary.
ENDLOOP.
```

stretch.brief: Delete the lowest-paid employee with `DELETE gt_emp INDEX n.` after finding which row it is in a loop (remember sy-tabix). Then print the remaining count.
stretch.solution: Track the minimum in a loop, store its `sy-tabix`, leave the loop, then `DELETE gt_emp INDEX lv_idx.` Imran (row 4) is deleted; lines( ) is then 4.

days.milestone: You can build a table from scratch, loop it, total it and update it correctly.

days.title: Checkpoint 1: foundations
days.goal: Prove the foundations: types, arithmetic and strings, loops, and internal tables. Pass mark 75%.
objectives: Answer 12 mixed questions without looking anything up
Write a small program from a blank editor
Fix whatever the result shows is weak before Phase B
days.read:
## How today works
Today is a **checkpoint**, not a new lesson. Phase B builds directly on Days 1–4, so anything shaky here would slow you down later.

1. **Skim** the four summaries below (8 minutes).
2. Write the **mini-program** from a blank editor (30 minutes). Look at hints only when stuck.
3. Take the **12-question test**. The pass mark is **75%** (9 of 12).
4. Anything you miss is reteaught and retested before Day 6 opens.

## Day 1 to 4 in one breath
- **Types:** `c` is length 1 unless you say LENGTH; `n` pads with zeros; `p` holds decimals; TYPES describes, DATA allocates, CONSTANTS never changes; `DATA(x) = …` takes its type from the right side.
- **Arithmetic and text:** into `i` a division is **rounded**; `DIV` cuts, `MOD` is the remainder; strings: templates, CONDENSE, strlen, offset/length, CS.
- **Control flow:** `sy-index` starts at 1; `EXIT` leaves the innermost loop; `CONTINUE` skips a pass; `CASE` needs `WHEN OTHERS`.
- **Tables:** `LOOP AT … INTO` **copies** the row; change the table with `MODIFY`; `sy-tabix` is the row number; `lines( )` counts rows.

exercise.title: Stock report from a blank editor
exercise.brief: Build one program that uses types, a structure, a table, CASE, CONTINUE and a total. No copying from earlier days.
steps: Create **ZABAP_D5**.
Define **ty_item** (id i, name c15, cat c1, qty i, price p 8,2), a constant **gc_low = 10**, and a standard table.
Add five items (id, name, cat, qty, price): (1 Keyboard E 25 19.99), (2 Notebook S 0 3.50), (3 Mouse E 8 9.50), (4 Pen S 120 0.80), (5 Monitor E 6 149.00).

Loop over the table. **Skip items with qty 0** using CONTINUE. For every other item print name, a **category word** chosen with CASE (E = Electronics, S = Stationery, anything else = Other), qty and the stock value (qty x price).
Add the stock values into a **total** and count items whose qty is **below gc_low**.
Print the total and the low-stock count. Activate and run.
hints: The value can be a p with 12 length and 2 decimals: `gv_val = gs_item-qty * gs_item-price.`
Put `IF gs_item-qty = 0. CONTINUE. ENDIF.` first in the loop, before any printing or adding.
The category word: `CASE gs_item-cat. WHEN 'E'. gv_cat = 'Electronics'. WHEN 'S'. gv_cat = 'Stationery'. WHEN OTHERS. gv_cat = 'Other'. ENDCASE.`
exercise.solution:
```abap
REPORT zabap_d5.

TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_item,
         id    TYPE i,
         name  TYPE c LENGTH 15,
         cat   TYPE c LENGTH 1,
         qty   TYPE i,
         price TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2,
       END OF ty_item.

CONSTANTS gc_low TYPE i VALUE 10.

DATA: gt_item  TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_item WITH EMPTY KEY,
      gs_item  TYPE ty_item,
      gv_val   TYPE p LENGTH 12 DECIMALS 2,
      gv_total TYPE p LENGTH 12 DECIMALS 2,
      gv_low   TYPE i,
      gv_cat   TYPE string.

APPEND VALUE #( id = 1 name = 'Keyboard' cat = 'E' qty = 25  price = '19.99' ) TO gt_item.
APPEND VALUE #( id = 2 name = 'Notebook' cat = 'S' qty = 0   price = '3.50'  ) TO gt_item.
APPEND VALUE #( id = 3 name = 'Mouse'    cat = 'E' qty = 8   price = '9.50'  ) TO gt_item.
APPEND VALUE #( id = 4 name = 'Pen'      cat = 'S' qty = 120 price = '0.80'  ) TO gt_item.
APPEND VALUE #( id = 5 name = 'Monitor'  cat = 'E' qty = 6   price = '149.00' ) TO gt_item.

LOOP AT gt_item INTO gs_item.
  IF gs_item-qty = 0.
    CONTINUE.
  ENDIF.
  CASE gs_item-cat.
    WHEN 'E'. gv_cat = 'Electronics'.
    WHEN 'S'. gv_cat = 'Stationery'.
    WHEN OTHERS. gv_cat = 'Other'.
  ENDCASE.
  gv_val = gs_item-qty * gs_item-price.
  gv_total = gv_total + gv_val.
  IF gs_item-qty < gc_low.
    gv_low = gv_low + 1.
  ENDIF.
  WRITE: / gs_item-name, gv_cat, gs_item-qty, gv_val.
ENDLOOP.

WRITE: / 'Total:', gv_total.
WRITE: / 'Low stock:', gv_low.
```

stretch.brief: Raise every price by 5% with MODIFY, then print the new total stock value. Predict it before you run it.
stretch.solution: Multiply by 105 / 100 in the loop and MODIFY. Because rounding to 2 decimals happens per item, compare your prediction with the program output and explain any cent differences.

days.milestone: Milestone 1: you can write a table-driven report from a blank editor and trace its output by hand.

d1.q1.prompt:
What does this print?
```abap
DATA gv TYPE c.
gv = 'ABC'.
WRITE gv.
```
d1.q1.why: TYPE c without LENGTH is exactly one character, so the text is cut to its first letter.

d1.q2.prompt:
What does this print?
```abap
DATA zip TYPE n LENGTH 5.
zip = '42'.
WRITE zip.
```
d1.q2.why: Type n is digit-text padded with leading zeros up to its length.

d1.q3.prompt:
Which line causes a syntax error?
```abap
CONSTANTS gc_max TYPE i VALUE 10.
DATA gv_n TYPE i.

gv_n = gc_max.      " line A
gc_max = 20.        " line B
gv_n = gv_n + 1.    " line C
```
d1.q3.why: A constant can be read but never assigned a new value.

d1.q4.prompt: What does `TYPES ty_amt TYPE p LENGTH 8 DECIMALS 2.` do?
options: Describes a type; no variable is created
d1.q4.why: TYPES only defines a shape. You need DATA to create something of that type.

d1.q5.prompt: Which statement correctly sets the name field of structure gs_emp?
d1.q5.why: Fields of a structure are reached with a dash.

d1.q6.prompt:
What is printed?
```abap
DATA(lv) = 'Hi'.
lv = 'Hello world'.
WRITE lv.
```
d1.q6.why: The literal 'Hi' makes lv a c of length 2, so the new text is cut to two characters.

d1.r1.prompt:
What does this print?
```abap
DATA a TYPE c LENGTH 3.
a = 'ABCDE'.
WRITE a.
```
d1.r1.why: The text is truncated to the declared length of 3.

d1.r2.prompt: Which statement declares a value that can never be changed?
d1.r2.why: CONSTANTS with VALUE is the fixed value; DATA stays changeable and TYPES creates no variable.

d1.r3.prompt: What is `gs_emp` after `DATA gs_emp TYPE ty_emp.` (ty_emp defined with BEGIN OF … END OF)?
options: One record holding all fields of ty_emp
d1.r3.why: A TYPE with BEGIN OF/END OF describes one row; DATA gives you one such row.

d1.r4.prompt:
What is the type of lv_n?
```abap
DATA(lv_n) = 10.
```
d1.r4.why: The literal 10 is an integer, so the inline variable gets type i.

d2.q1.prompt:
What is stored in gv_int?
```abap
DATA gv_int TYPE i.
gv_int = 7 / 2.
```
d2.q1.why: ABAP rounds the result when it is stored in an integer, so 3.5 becomes 4.

d2.q2.prompt:
What is stored in gv_int?
```abap
DATA gv_int TYPE i.
gv_int = 10 / 4.
```
d2.q2.why: 2.5 is rounded to the nearest whole number, away from zero: 3.

d2.q3.prompt: What do `17 DIV 5` and `17 MOD 5` give, in that order?
d2.q3.why: DIV is the whole quotient (3 fives) and MOD the remainder (17 - 15 = 2).

d2.q4.prompt: You need the result 3.50 from 7 / 2. What must change?
options: Declare the target as p with 2 decimals
d2.q4.why: An i variable can only hold whole numbers; a p with DECIMALS can hold 3.50.

d2.q5.prompt:
What does `WRITE strlen( lv ).` show after this?
```abap
DATA lv TYPE string VALUE `  a   b  `.
CONDENSE lv.
```
d2.q5.why: CONDENSE trims the ends and reduces inner spaces to one, leaving "a b" with 3 characters.

d2.q6.prompt:
What does this print?
```abap
DATA lv TYPE c LENGTH 7 VALUE 'SAPABAP'.
WRITE lv+3(4).
```
d2.q6.why: Offset 3 skips S, A, P; length 4 takes A, B, A, P.

d2.r1.prompt:
What is stored in gv_int?
```abap
DATA gv_int TYPE i.
gv_int = 9 / 2.
```
d2.r1.why: 4.5 is rounded up to 5 when stored in an integer.

d2.r2.prompt: Which expression is true only for even numbers?
d2.r2.why: An even number has no remainder when divided by 2.

d2.r3.prompt: Which line produces "Hello Deepak" if lv_name = 'Deepak'?
d2.r3.why: Only a string template with curly braces inserts the variable value.

d2.r4.why: CS (contains string) is not case-sensitive, so VOICE matches the voice inside invoice.

d3.q1.prompt:
What is the last number printed?
```abap
DO 4 TIMES.
  WRITE: / sy-index.
ENDDO.
```
d3.q1.why: sy-index starts at 1, so four passes print 1, 2, 3, 4.

d3.q2.prompt:
What happens with this loop?
```abap
DO.
  WRITE: / sy-index.
ENDDO.
```
options: It does not stop on its own (until the program times out)
d3.q2.why: A plain DO has no pass count. It needs an EXIT or similar to end.

d3.q3.prompt:
How many lines are written?
```abap
DO 3 TIMES.
  DO 5 TIMES.
    IF sy-index = 3.
      EXIT.
    ENDIF.
    WRITE: / sy-index.
  ENDDO.
ENDDO.
```
d3.q3.why: EXIT leaves only the inner loop. Each inner loop writes indexes 1 and 2, three times: 6 lines.

d3.q4.prompt: What does `CONTINUE.` do inside a loop?
options: Skips the rest of this pass and starts the next one
d3.q4.why: CONTINUE jumps to the next pass; EXIT is the one that leaves.

d3.q5.prompt:
What is printed?
```abap
DATA gv TYPE i VALUE 30.
IF gv > 10.
  WRITE: / 'A'.
ELSEIF gv > 20.
  WRITE: / 'B'.
ELSE.
  WRITE: / 'C'.
ENDIF.
```
d3.q5.why: The first true condition wins and later branches are skipped, even if they are also true.

d3.q6.prompt: Inside the inner DO, what does sy-index hold?
options: The pass count of the outer loop
The pass count of the inner loop
d3.q6.why: Each loop level has its own counter. Save the outer value in a variable if you need it.

d3.r1.prompt: How many passes does `DO 0 TIMES.` make?
d3.r1.why: Zero passes means the body is never entered.

d3.r2.prompt: Which statement skips to the next pass if a condition is false?
d3.r2.why: CHECK continues only when its condition is true, otherwise it moves to the next pass.

d3.r3.prompt: Which keyword covers all values not named in earlier WHEN branches?
d3.r3.why: In a CASE statement the catch-all branch is WHEN OTHERS.

d3.r4.prompt: An outer DO 4 TIMES contains an inner DO 3 TIMES with no EXIT. How many times does the inner body run in total?
d3.r4.why: Three passes for each of four outer passes: 4 x 3 = 12.

d4.q1.prompt:
After this code, what is the salary of the first row in gt_emp (it was 1000)?
```abap
LOOP AT gt_emp INTO gs_emp.
  gs_emp-salary = gs_emp-salary + 500.
ENDLOOP.
```
d4.q1.why: INTO copies the row into the work area. Changing the copy does not touch the table.

d4.q2.prompt: Which addition makes the change persist?
options: MODIFY gt_emp FROM gs_emp. inside the loop
APPEND gs_emp TO gt_emp. inside the loop
d4.q2.why: MODIFY writes the work area back to the current row. APPEND would add a duplicate row.

d4.q3.prompt: What is `gs_emp` in `DATA gs_emp TYPE ty_emp.`?
options: A work area that holds a single row
A pointer to the first row
d4.q3.why: The work area is a single-row structure used to move one row at a time.

options: The index of the last row only if the table is sorted
The number of rows in the table
d4.q4.why: lines( ) counts the rows currently in the table.

d4.q5.prompt: Inside `LOOP AT gt_emp INTO gs_emp WHERE salary > 50000.` the matching rows are 2, 3 and 5. What is sy-tabix on the third match?
d4.q5.why: sy-tabix is the row number in the table, so the third matching row has tabix 5.

d4.q6.prompt: What happens to the row numbers after `DELETE gt_emp INDEX 2.` on a 4-row table?
options: Former rows 3 and 4 become rows 2 and 3
They stay the same and row 2 is empty
d4.q6.why: Rows below the deleted one move up by one, so the table stays contiguous.

d4.r1.prompt: Which statement adds a new last row to gt_emp using the work area gs_emp?
d4.r1.why: APPEND ... TO appends a work area as the last row.

d4.r2.prompt: Why can `gs_emp-salary = gs_emp-salary * 2.` in a LOOP … INTO leave the table unchanged?
options: gs_emp is a copy of the row
d4.r2.why: The loop copies each row into the work area, so only the copy is changed.

d4.r3.prompt: Which statement removes every row with a salary under 40000?
d4.r3.why: DELETE itab WHERE deletes all matching rows in one statement.

d4.r4.prompt: What is sy-subrc after a LOOP over an empty table?
d4.r4.why: If no row is processed, the loop ends with sy-subrc = 4.

d5.q1.prompt:
What is printed?
```abap
DATA n TYPE n LENGTH 3.
n = 12345.
WRITE n.
```
d5.q1.why: Numeric text keeps the rightmost digits when the value is too long, so only 345 fits.

d5.q2.prompt: You want to change the length of every amount field in a program in one place. What is the best design?
options: Declare each field with its own LENGTH
TYPES ty_amt once, then DATA ... TYPE ty_amt for each variable
d5.q2.why: A shared TYPES is the single point of change for all variables built from it.

d5.q3.prompt:
What is printed?
```abap
DATA(lv_name) = 'Deepak'.
lv_name = 'Deepak Raj'.
WRITE lv_name.
```
d5.q3.why: The inline variable is a c of length 6 (the length of the literal), so the longer text is cut.

d5.q4.prompt:
What does gv_int contain?
```abap
DATA gv_int TYPE i.
gv_int = 5 / 2.
```
d5.q4.why: 2.5 is rounded up to 3 when stored in an integer.

d5.q5.prompt:
What does gv_r hold?
```abap
DATA gv_r TYPE i.
gv_r = 20 MOD 6.
```

d5.q6.prompt:
What is printed?
```abap
DATA lv TYPE c LENGTH 14 VALUE 'ABAP Developer'.
WRITE lv+5(3).
```
d5.q6.why: Offset 5 skips A, B, A, P and the space; length 3 takes D, e, v.

d5.q7.prompt:
How many lines are written?
```abap
DO 2 TIMES.
  DO 4 TIMES.
    IF sy-index = 3.
      EXIT.
    ENDIF.
    WRITE: / sy-index.
  ENDDO.
ENDDO.
```
d5.q7.why: EXIT stops only the inner loop at its third pass: 2 lines per outer pass, 2 outer passes.

d5.q8.prompt:
What does gv hold at the end?
```abap
DATA gv TYPE i VALUE 10.
DO 3 TIMES.
  gv = gv + sy-index.
ENDDO.
```

d5.q9.prompt:
What is printed?
```abap
DATA gv_c TYPE c LENGTH 1 VALUE 'B'.
CASE gv_c.
  WHEN 'A'. WRITE 1.
  WHEN 'B'. WRITE 2.
  WHEN 'C'. WRITE 3.
  WHEN OTHERS. WRITE 4.
ENDCASE.
```
d5.q9.why: A CASE runs only the matching WHEN branch; it does not fall through.

d5.q10.prompt:
The first row of gt has qty 7. What is it afterwards?
```abap
LOOP AT gt INTO gs.
  gs-qty = 0.
  MODIFY gt FROM gs.
ENDLOOP.
```
d5.q10.why: MODIFY writes the changed work area back to the current row.

d5.q11.prompt: What is sy-subrc after a LOOP that processed at least one row?
d5.q11.why: sy-subrc is 0 if the loop body ran at least once.

d5.q12.prompt:
What does lines( gt ) return?
```abap
" gt has 3 rows
DELETE gt INDEX 1.
```
d5.q12.why: One row was removed from three, so two remain.

d5.r1.prompt:
What is printed?
```abap
DATA x TYPE c LENGTH 2.
x = 'XYZ'.
WRITE x.
```
d5.r1.why: Text is cut to the declared length of 2.

d5.r2.prompt: Which statement creates a variable that can change?
d5.r2.why: Only DATA creates a variable whose value can change; CONSTANTS is fixed and TYPES is just a shape.

d5.r3.why: Only a p with DECIMALS can hold a fraction.

d5.r4.prompt: Which statement removes extra spaces from lv?
d5.r4.why: CONDENSE trims the ends and reduces inner space runs to one.

d5.r5.prompt: Which statement leaves only the innermost loop?
d5.r5.why: EXIT ends the loop it is directly in.

d5.r6.prompt: Why do we write `MODIFY gt FROM gs.` in a LOOP … INTO?
options: Because gs is only a copy of the table row
d5.r6.why: The work area is a copy; MODIFY is what updates the real row.
